newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN T-BILL YIELD RECORD LOW ON HIGH DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN T-BILL YIELD RECORD LOW ON HIGH DEMAND.

text.p: The annualised average yield on an issue of 364-day Russian GKO discount Treasury bills hit historical lows at an auction on Wednesday on high investment demand, dealers said.
But poor demand on an OFZ bond pushed the yield up, as the Finance Ministry satisfied even the most aggressive bids, they said.
They forecast a stable market in the next few days due to high overnight credit rates.
"The Finance Ministry sold the one-year paper a bit lower than the market yield level," said United City Bank dealer Stanislav Kuchinsky.
"The demand was high most likely because the big volume of repayment...was re-invested into the new paper by non-residents."
Banks bid a total 9.77 trillion roubles for an eight trillion rouble T-bill auction. The yield was 18.68 percent.
Bids for a 10.00 trillion rouble OFZ bond auction were 3.83 trillion roubles. The yield was 25.19 percent.
The Finance Ministry repaid 6.81 trillion roubles on a maturing T-bill, paid 412.6 billion roubles in interest on series 22073 bond and 5.33 trillion roubles in early repayment on the bond.
"The Finance Ministry had to do something to raise funds for refinancing and sold the OFZ bond with a good premium, so that it is...interesting from a speculative point of view," a dealer said.
